title: Slow recognition of overseas-trained health practitioners
summary: Overseas-trained doctors, nurses and other health practitioners face long and costly assessments before they can practise; for specialist doctors, the medical colleges assess comparability. An independent review for National Cabinet (the Kruk review, endorsed December 2023) made 28 recommendations to speed and simplify registration.
direction_rationale: Slow, costly recognition narrows the pool of practitioners in a workforce with shortages, and lets incumbent professional bodies control the pace of entry.

assessment.summary: Overseas-trained health practitioners wait a long time, and pay a lot, to be recognised, with specialist colleges assessing their peers. It holds back supply in one of the largest workforces.
